pharm: Selective, reversible inhibitor of JAK1/JAK2 that blocks cytokine signaling through the JAK-STAT pathway, dampening inflammatory and immune responses.
quick: RA: 2 mg PO once daily; COVID-19: 4 mg once daily; alopecia areata: 2-4 mg once daily
May cause fetal harm (animal data); weigh risk/benefit
Not recommended; advise not to breastfeed
Reduce or avoid by eGFR and indication (see renal)
No specific interaction; consider hepatic risk
TB/hepatitis screen, CBC, LFTs, lipids, signs of infection/thrombosis/MACE
summary: Baricitinib is an oral once-daily JAK inhibitor used for refractory rheumatoid arthritis, hospitalized COVID-19 requiring oxygen support, and severe alopecia areata. It carries a BOXED WARNING for serious (sometimes fatal) infections including tuberculosis, increased all-cause mortality, malignancy (lymphoma, lung cancer), major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and thrombosis (DVT, PE, arterial). Screen for active/latent TB and viral hepatitis and check baseline blood counts before starting, and monitor closely throughout. Dose must be reduced for renal impairment and avoided in severe hepatic impairment.
indications: Moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis in adults with inadequate response to one or more TNF blockers
COVID-19 in hospitalized adults requiring supplemental oxygen, non-invasive or invasive mechanical ventilation, or ECMO
Limitation of use: not recommended with other JAK inhibitors, biologic DMARDs/immunomodulators, or potent immunosuppressants (e.g., azathioprine, cyclosporine)

dosage.n: Monotherapy or with methotrexate/other non-biologic DMARDs

dosage.t: Once daily for up to 14 days
dosage.n: Continue for 14 days or until hospital discharge, whichever is first

dosage.d: 2 mg; increase to 4 mg if inadequate response
dosage.n: Consider 4 mg for near-complete/complete scalp loss; reduce to 2 mg once adequate response achieved
If recommended dose is 1 mg, consider discontinuing probenecid

dosage.d: Same mg dose dispersed in room-temperature water
dosage.n: Dispersed tablets stable in water up to 4 hours; use water volume/rinse per route

admin: Before starting: evaluate for active and latent TB; do not give with active TB; treat latent TB first (except COVID-19)
Screen for viral hepatitis and obtain baseline CBC, hepatic and renal function; update immunizations (RA/AA)
Take once daily with or without food
For patients unable to swallow, disperse tablet(s) in room-temperature water for oral, G-tube, or NG/OG-tube administration
Do not initiate if ALC <500, ANC <1000, or hemoglobin <8 g/dL (RA/AA); for COVID-19 if ALC <200 or ANC <500
moa: Inhibits Janus kinases (JAK1 and JAK2), intracellular enzymes that transmit cytokine and growth-factor receptor signals. By preventing JAK-mediated phosphorylation and activation of STAT transcription factors, baricitinib reduces the signaling of multiple proinflammatory cytokines, modulating immune and hematopoietic cell function.

relative: Active serious or opportunistic infection, including localized infection
Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m2 in RA/AA)
Patients at high risk of thrombosis (DVT/PE/arterial)
History of MACE, current/past smokers (higher malignancy and MACE risk)
Concurrent live vaccines or other JAK inhibitors/biologic DMARDs
monitor: Active/latent TB before and during therapy
Signs/symptoms of infection, thrombosis, and cardiovascular events

preg: Based on animal reproduction studies, baricitinib may cause fetal harm (skeletal malformations, reduced fetal weight, embryolethality in rabbits at multiples of the human dose); human data are insufficient. Weigh risks and benefits of chronic use during pregnancy; report exposures to the manufacturer pregnancy registry.
lact: Presence in human milk and effects on the breastfed infant are unknown; advise patients not to breastfeed during treatment and for an appropriate period afterward.
renal: RA and alopecia areata: 2 mg once daily for mild impairment (eGFR 60-<90), 1 mg once daily for moderate (eGFR 30-<60), not recommended if eGFR <30. COVID-19: 4 mg for eGFR 60-<90, 2 mg for 30-<60, 1 mg for 15-<30, not recommended if eGFR <15 (ESRD, dialysis, or acute kidney injury). Substantially renally excreted.
hepatic: Not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment (RA and alopecia areata); not studied in COVID-19 with severe hepatic impairment. Interrupt if ALT/AST rise and drug-induced liver injury is suspected, until DILI is excluded.

major: Other JAK inhibitors and biologic DMARDs/immunomodulators (not studied; avoid combination)
Potent immunosuppressants such as azathioprine and cyclosporine (avoid)
moderate: Strong OAT3 inhibitors (e.g., probenecid) increase baricitinib exposure - halve the dose
minor: Substrate of P-gp, BCRP, OAT3, and MATE2-K transporters
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal slightly lowers AUC/Cmax without clinical relevance.
interactions.alcohol: No specific drug interaction documented; consider additive hepatic risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Obtain baseline and periodic CBC, hepatic enzymes, lipids; latent TB and viral hepatitis screening before initiation.

serious: Serious bacterial, fungal, viral and opportunistic infections including tuberculosis (boxed warning)
Malignancy including lymphoma and lung cancer (boxed warning)
Major adverse cardiovascular events - cardiovascular death, MI, stroke (boxed warning)
Thrombosis - DVT, pulmonary embolism, arterial thrombosis (boxed warning)
Increased all-cause and sudden cardiovascular mortality (boxed warning)
rare: Reactivation of latent viral infections (CMV, BK virus, histoplasmosis, cryptococcosis)
emergency: Pulmonary embolism or symptomatic thrombosis (discontinue and evaluate promptly)

monitoring: Active and latent tuberculosis before and during therapy (except COVID-19 before initiation)
CBC: absolute lymphocyte count, absolute neutrophil count, hemoglobin at baseline and during treatment
Renal function (eGFR) and dose adjust accordingly
Ongoing signs/symptoms of infection, thrombosis (DVT/PE), and cardiovascular events; new abdominal symptoms for GI perforation
counsel: This medicine carries serious risks of infection, blood clots, heart events, and cancer; report fever, cough, leg swelling, chest pain, shortness of breath, or sudden weakness immediately
Tell your clinician about any current or recent infection, prior TB, hepatitis, smoking history, or clotting problems
Do not receive live vaccines while on treatment
Take once daily with or without food; do not combine with other JAK inhibitors or strong immunosuppressants
Do not breastfeed; discuss pregnancy plans with your clinician
pk: Peak plasma at ~1 hour; steady state in 2-3 days
~12-16 h (RA/alopecia areata); ~10.8 h in intubated COVID-19 patients
20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); keep out of reach of children
pearls: Boxed warning class effect for JAK inhibitors: serious infection, mortality, malignancy, MACE, and thrombosis - extrapolated largely from another JAK inhibitor vs TNF blockers in RA patients >=50 with a cardiovascular risk factor
Always screen and treat latent TB and check viral hepatitis before starting (except COVID-19 before initiation)
Halve the dose with strong OAT3 inhibitors such as probenecid
Avoid live vaccines; not for use with other JAK inhibitors, biologic DMARDs, or potent immunosuppressants
Discontinue permanently after an MI or stroke; stop and evaluate promptly for suspected thrombosis
~80% oral bioavailability; substantially renally cleared, so dose by eGFR
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular once-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Single doses up to 40 mg and multiple doses of 20 mg/day for 10 days were given in trials without dose-limiting toxicity; over 90% of a dose is eliminated within 24 hours. No specific antidote - monitor for adverse reactions and provide supportive, symptom-directed treatment.
